The main factual issue is the 3D bounding box count: the card states 64,595 (matching the IEEE Xplore abstract) while the official Princeton project page and paper PDF state 58,657 — a known version discrepancy. The HuggingFace repo listed (wyrx/SUNRGBD_seg) is a community-derived segmentation dataset, not the canonical benchmark repo, making it a contamination risk. The leaderboard scores from llm-stats.com reference real Qwen3.5 models. No fabricated facts were found. Overall verdict: minor issues only.
author_notes: The repo is one user's segmentation-only rework of the data. The real benchmark is only distributed via the Princeton project page.

screen_summary: The ChartQA card is largely accurate: correct benchmark identity, correct paper (arxiv 2203.10244), correct authors, correct dataset statistics (9.6K human + 23.1K machine questions, 20,882 charts), and correct baseline numbers (VisionTaPas 49.80%, VL-T5 45.82% on ChartQA; 94.54% on DVQA; 61.04% human agreement). The main issues are: (1) the HF repo listed (lmms-lab/ChartQA) is a reformatted secondary version for lmms-eval, not the canonical original from vis-nlp, and org_url incorrectly points to lmms-lab; (2) the DVQA 94.54% result is presented as a ChartQA baseline when it is actually a result on a different benchmark; (3) the data size field ('1K to 10K') understates the true total of ~32.7K questions; (4) MTurk compensation details are misplaced in the interpretation field. No fabricated facts were found.
author_notes: The lmms-lab README itself says it is a reformatted version for lmms-eval, and the card even uses lmms-lab as the org URL.
